data.why: FigureLab's 'Load example figure' button (id=load-example-btn, calls loadExampleFigure()) generates a labelled, scale-barred demo figure entirely client-side in JS, so no upload files are needed to exercise the full workflow.

goals: Assemble a multi-panel figure (e.g. a 2x2 fluorescence grid or a western blot with loading control) from raw images into a grid layout
Calibrate and add scale bars that remain numerically correct after cropping
Adjust brightness, contrast, gamma and LUTs per panel and standardize settings across all panels
Annotate the figure with arrows, rulers, insets, text labels and panel letters
Run the Deep Figure Audit and Exposure Analysis to catch inconsistent LUTs, missing scale bars, overexposure, and duplicate panels before submission
Export a publication-ready figure (TIFF/PNG/PDF/SVG) at a target DPI and printed width, with reproducibility metadata embedded

review.summary: The tree states FigureLab's purpose exactly and walks the README's own section order, with screens that check out. It misses the blot/gel half of the tool and true display-setting standardisation, mislabels histogram auto-stretch as standardising, and needs a few feature boundaries tidied before it is filed.
